Container.Name: cairn
Container.Overview:
Shared, persistent project memory for AI coding agents. Agents such as Claude Code record what they learn about a project (conventions, traps, decisions, handoffs) in your own Neo4j, and any agent on any machine starts from a compact briefing instead of re-reading the repository.
Serves an MCP endpoint at /mcp and a dashboard at /ui/ (live request feed, memory graph, projects, access control). The server calls no LLM and needs no API key.
On first start the container log prints a one-time setup code: open the WebUI, enter it and create the admin account. Create one access token per computer in the dashboard (Access). Requires a Neo4j 5 database that the container can reach; there is no appdata, all memory lives in Neo4j. Use plain http:// on your LAN, or put a TLS reverse proxy or VPN in front before exposing it further.
Container.Requires: A running Neo4j 5 (for example the Neo4j template from Community Applications). Set its password first, then enter the address and password below.

Config.Name: Neo4j URI
Config.Description: Bolt address of your Neo4j, for example bolt://SERVER-IP:7687. Inside a container localhost is the container itself, so use an address it can reach.

Config.Name: Neo4j password
Config.Description: Neo4j password. Change Neo4j's default password; the dashboard's System page warns while it is still the default.

Config.Name: Static token (optional)
Config.Description: Normally leave empty and create tokens in the dashboard (Access).

Config.Name: Capture mode
Config.Description: full keeps request and response payloads in memory for the dashboard's Live view; meta keeps only a summary. Nothing is written to disk.

Config.Name: Behind a reverse proxy
Config.Description: Set to 1 only if a proxy you control sets X-Forwarded-For.

Config.Name: Secure cookies (HTTPS)
Config.Description: Set to 1 when the dashboard is served over HTTPS (behind a TLS proxy). Leave empty for plain http://.
